decisions.reason: The title unnecessarily describes the reference row as iid, whereas the stated result correctly permits a common square-integrable law with pairwise zero covariances. Joint exchangeability transfers the L2 coupling bound to every coordinate. Holder bounds the difference of pairwise covariances by quantities tending to zero, and the exchangeable-mean variance is Var(X_1)/N+(1-1/N)Cov(X_1,X_2). Together with convergence of the means this proves the stated L2 conclusion without independence. Corrected only the title to describe uncorrelated reference rows; the Statement and proof remain unchanged.

The Definition omitted the positive-dimension admissibility condition even though its empty-boundary contract says d,p>=1, def-data-assimilation-problem uses positive state/observation dimensions, and its well-definedness theorem assumes d,p>=1. Taken literally at p=0 its Cholesky call is outside the supplier Statement n>=1. Added only the explicit integers d,p>=1 convention already required by those interfaces; no formula, output or intended positive-dimensional claim was weakened. For p>=1, S is symmetric positive definite and both triangular systems are uniquely solvable, yielding S K^T=HB and the stated gain.

The rejection overlooks the existing Facts & Assumptions: its Given fixes the one-dimensional Gaussian prior/error model, F1 explicitly states independent Gaussian initial and observation errors and links the independent-noise model, and verification step 2.1 expressly selects that independent model. Under this setup take T=1, X_0~N(0,1), F_1=1, Q_1=0, H_1=R_1=1 and independent r_1. Then S=2, K=1/2, m^a=1, P^a=1/2; completing the square gives J=(u-1)^2+1. The cited exact-filter theorem supplies the Gaussian conditional-law version N(1,1/2). The proposed correlation-1/2 witness has Var(Y)=3 and posterior variance 1/4, but violates the explicitly independent-noise setup of F1 and step 2.1. No mathematical repair to this item is warranted.
